newsitem.title: USA: April retail sales weaken from March.
newsitem.headline: April retail sales weaken from March.

text.p: Sales at retail stores were down broadly in April, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, partly because of weaker demand for new cars and a slower pace of department-store sales.

Total retail sales declined last month by 0.3 percent to a seasonally adjusted $212.2 billion -- the largest drop since June last year -- after a revision to show flat sales in March instead of a 0.1 percent pickup.
The falloff in April sales was widespread and included continued declines in furniture sales as well as drops in sales of clothing, food and gasoline.

The report confirmed other indications that consumer demand lost some steam during April. The monthly sales pace for domestic new cars eased to its slowest rate since mid-1995 and chain store sales fell from March as consumers apparently took a breather from stores and showrooms.

"We had an extraordinary first quarter for retail sales, ... so April's decline represents perhaps more of a correction than signalling a fundamental deterioration for household expenditures," said John Lonski, senior economist at Moody's Investors Service.
Sales of new cars were down 0.9 percent to a seasonally adjusted $51.9 billion following a 0.3 percent March decline. It was the steepest drop in new-car sales since a 1.2 percent fall last November.

New cars account for about one-quarter of total retail sales, so swings in demand strongly affect the overall monthly figures. Excluding cars, retail sales were down 0.1 percent last month after a 0.1 percent rise in March.

Sales by general merchandise stores fell 0.9 percent in April to $27.2 billion after a 0.1 percent decline in March. At apparel stores, sales of clothing declined 0.6 percent to $9.6 billion after a 1 percent drop in March.

Sales of building materials were flat in April at $12 billion after a 1 percent jump in March. Analysts said beforehand that unseasonable weather and flooding in parts of the country likely slowed building activity.
Gasoline service station sales decreased by 0.1 percent in April to $13.3 billion following a 0.5 percent decline in March. Prices for gasoline were lower in April than in March.

The signs of tapering consumer demand come before next Tuesday's policy-setting session of the Federal Open Market Committee. The Fed boosted short-term rates by a quarter percentage point in March, citing concern that strong demand risked firing up inflationary price and wage rises.
